newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up on less-than-expected imports.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up on less-than-expected imports.

text.p: The won closed a little higher against the dollar on Friday as less import settlements appeared than expected, traders said.
The won stood at 828.40 at the close after opening at 828.80. It ranged between 827.80 and 829.20.
"The dollar continued to be weak as expected import deals failed to materialise," said a dealer at Korea First Bank.
Dealers said the dollar's weakness against the Japanese yen in world markets and expected month-end export negotiations also helped the won's rise.
However, they added that the market was slightly short in dollars which prevented the won from moving much higher.
The won is likely to move in a range of 827.00 to 829.00 on Monday.
"End of the month export deals will continue to pressure the dollar next week," said the First Bank dealer.
